$comment: The dashboard's note on what Agent Cake records and how it decides (/api/overview serves it). Each row's 'how it's decided' is the sentence of a class in judging.en.json, named by 'class' ('named': how an agent's name is found): the same words the verdicts use, never a copy. 'verdict' is the row's level 1, whose badge it shows. The names of the categories are judging.en.json's (the dashboard's categories block). {name} is the product name (product.json). English only; visitors are Human or Agent; no comparison with any other product.
title: What {name} records
lead: {name} classifies each session on this computer, when new activity arrives and again when the session goes inactive. It doesn't call any AI service.

rows.what: A browser extension, an AI browser, or a cloud agent, like Claude in Chrome, Comet, or ChatGPT agent
rows.shown_as: Agent, named when the evidence identifies it

rows.what: The built-in browser of an AI desktop app, or a cloud agent that gives its name
rows.shown_as: Agent, identified by name, such as Codex browser

rows.what: An automated browser that doesn't give its name, like Playwright, Puppeteer, or Selenium
rows.shown_as: Agent, identified by the tool's name when its traces show it, otherwise Unnamed

rows.what: A program that gives its name and isn't an agent: a search engine, a monitor, a link preview
rows.shown_as: Counted only; “Verified” when a signature or the operator's published address range confirms it

rows.what: A human and an agent taking turns
rows.shown_as: Human + agent, split at each hand-off

rows.what: Too few actions, or a phone or tablet
rows.shown_as: Human, marked Thin evidence, with the reason

rows.what: Evidence that's too weak or points both ways
rows.shown_as: Human, marked Thin evidence, with the reason

bot.question: What counts as a bot
bot.answer: A bot is a program that names itself and is known to have no human behind it, such as a search engine, a monitor, or a link preview. A visitor that only seems automated counts as an Agent, never a Bot.

average_length: Measured from a session's first activity to its last, where activity is a page opening or any input, including pointer moves. Time a tab stays open afterward doesn't count. The session list shows each recording's full length, from its start to its last event.
